facts.statement: Notohypsilophodon is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina.
facts.quote: Notohypsilophodon (meaning "southern Hypsilophodon") is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina.

facts.statement: The species was named and described by Rubén D. Martínez in 1998.
facts.quote: In 1998 this find was named and described by Rubén D. Martínez as the type species Notohypsilophodon comodorensis.

facts.statement: The specific name refers to the city of Comodoro Rivadavia.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to Comodoro Rivadavia.

facts.statement: The describer considered the individual a juvenile because its neural arches were not fused to the vertebrae bodies.
facts.quote: Because the neural arches are not fused to the bodies of the vertebrae, its describer regarded the individual as not fully grown.
As a "hypsilophodontid" or other basal ornithopod, Notohypsilophodon would have been a bipedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the animal's length at 1.3 meters and its weight at 6 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul gave an estimation of 1.3 m for the length, 6 kg for the weight of the animal.

facts.statement: A recent redescription found Notohypsilophodon to be basal in Ornithopoda and more primitive than Gasparinisaura.
facts.quote: A recent redescription of Notohypsilophodon found it to be basal in Ornithopoda, more primitive than Gasparinisaura.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Notohypsilophodon was the only hypsilophodont known from South America, as Gasparinisaura is now considered a basal euornithopod as well.
facts.quote: It was described as the only "hypsilophodont" known from South America, although this assessment is not universally supported, and Gasparinisaura is now believed to have been a basal euornithopod as well.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue the fossil remains are too fragmentary to classify beyond Euornithopoda, a clade including hypsilophodonts and iguanodonts.
facts.quote: a more recent review of basal ornithopods found the fossil remains to be too fragmentary for classification beyond Euornithopoda, a clade within Ornithopoda including the "hypsilophodonts" and iguanodonts.

facts.statement: Notohypsilophodon lived from 100.5 to 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)

rejected.quote: At Buen Pasto near Comodoro Rivadavia a partial juvenile skeleton lacking the skull, was found.
